Front: What structural corruption occurs in HashMap if you override equals() but not hashCode()?
Back: Logical duplicate keys can end up in different bucket indices, making retrieval of existing elements fail (returns null) and causing duplicate key-value entries.

Front: Why does TreeSet/TreeMap ignore equals() for duplicate detection?
Back: It relies entirely on comparison results (compareTo() or compare() returning 0) to determine duplicates and position nodes within its Red-Black tree.

Front: What is the runtime complexity of adding an element to TreeSet?
Back: O(log N) because it must traverse the self-balancing Red-Black binary search tree.

Front: Why does ConcurrentHashMap reject null keys and null values?
Back: To avoid ambiguity in concurrent environments: preventing a race condition where calling containsKey() after get() returns null cannot tell if the key has a null value or is absent.

Front: How does ConcurrentHashMap achieve thread safety without locking the entire map for additions?
Back: It uses Compare-And-Swap (CAS) to insert nodes into empty buckets, and synchronizes only on the head node of the target bucket for write collisions.

Front: What is the key difference between Collections.unmodifiableList() and List.copyOf()?
Back: unmodifiableList returns a read-only wrapper view pointing to the live backing list, whereas List.copyOf returns a fully isolated, immutable copy.
